name: Parc Monceau
short_description: Romantic English-style public park in the 8th arrondissement, created in 1778 and famous for its scattered architectural follies including a Roman colonnade and miniature Egyptian pyramid.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Site of the world's first silk parachute jump in 1797 by Andre-Jacques Garnerin and the first public park created by Haussmann; rich for Hidden History and Nature & Green Spaces lenses.

name: Place du Tertre
short_description: Historic square at the summit of Montmartre where roughly 140 licensed artists work in one-square-meter pitches assigned by jury.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Former village square of Montmartre opened in 1635, central to the bohemian art scene from the late 18th century until WWI; high tourist traffic and strong Art & Street Culture lens potential.

name: Palais de Justice
short_description: Vast judicial complex on the Ile de la Cite occupying the former medieval royal palace of the kings of France and housing the Court of Cassation, France's highest ordinary court.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Continuous seat of French justice and royal power since the Capetians; shares its complex with Sainte-Chapelle and the Conciergerie, anchoring War & Revolution and Hidden History lenses.

name: Square du Vert-Galant
short_description: Triangular pocket-park at the western tip of Ile de la Cite, sitting roughly seven meters below modern street level and pointing downstream beneath the Pont Neuf.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Created in 1884 by joining the former Ile aux Juifs (where Jacques de Molay was burned in 1314) to Ile de la Cite; nicknamed for the amorous reputation of Henri IV, whose equestrian statue stands above. Strong Hidden History and Local Legends lens material.

name: Rue Saint-Honoré
short_description: Two-kilometer medieval street running west from the Louvre, lined with luxury boutiques and historic addresses including the house at no. 398 where Robespierre lodged before the guillotine.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Joan of Arc was wounded at the former Porte Saint-Honore in 1429 (plaque at no. 163) and Robespierre lived at no. 398 with the Duplay family; strong Revolution, Literary and Shopping lens density.

name: Crédit Municipal de Paris
short_description: Paris's oldest financial institution, a municipal pawnbroker re-established by Louis XVI in 1777 and renamed from Mont-de-Piété to Crédit Municipal de Paris by decree on 24 October 1918.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Inaugurated on this Marais site on 9 February 1778 with a Louis XVI-style extension by Charles-Francois Viel; nicknamed 'Chez ma tante' after Prince de Joinville's pawned watch. Distinctive Social Change and Hidden History lens material.

name: Tour Saint-Jacques
short_description: Lone 52-meter Flamboyant Gothic bell tower built 1509-1523, the only surviving fragment of the church of Saint-Jacques-de-la-Boucherie demolished in 1797.

_pipeline.address: Square de la Tour Saint-Jacques, 39 Rue de Rivoli, 75004 Paris
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Spared in 1793 as a condition of the church's sale, restored in the Second Empire and reputed starting point of the medieval Camino de Santiago pilgrimage from Paris; strong Religious & Spiritual and Historic Architecture lenses.

name: Rue de la Ferronnerie
short_description: Narrow former ironmongers' street where King Henri IV was assassinated by Francois Ravaillac on 14 May 1610, marked today by a commemorative stone in the pavement at no. 11.

discovery_sources: Un Jour de Plus à Paris
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Site of one of France's most consequential regicides; the carriage was halted by a wine-cart traffic jam beside the old Saints-Innocents cemetery. Anchor for Dark History and War & Revolution lenses.

name: Rue Saint-Antoine
short_description: Wide Gallo-Roman-origin artery in the Marais once called the 'most beautiful street in Paris' for its 17th-century hôtels particuliers, including the Hôtel de Sully at no. 62.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: King Henry II was fatally wounded in a tournament on this street in 1559; later the route of royal entries and an axis from the Bastille to the Hotel de Ville. Rich for Historic Architecture and War & Revolution lenses.

name: Quai d'Anjou
short_description: Northern quay of Ile Saint-Louis lined with 17th-century hôtels particuliers, several designed by Louis Le Vau before his work at Vaux-le-Vicomte and Versailles.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: The Hotel de Lauzun at no. 17 hosted the Club des Hashischins (Baudelaire, Gautier, Delacroix) in the 1840s; one of the best-preserved 17th-century streetscapes in Paris. Strong Literary & Film and Historic Architecture lenses.

name: Place des Abbesses
short_description: Lively Montmartre square fronted by one of only two surviving glass-canopied 'dragonfly' Metro entrances designed by Hector Guimard, salvaged in 1974 from the Hotel de Ville station.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Named for the abbesses of the medieval Montmartre Abbey; the adjoining station entry is the deepest in the Paris network at 36 m below street level. Anchors Modern & Contemporary Design and Historic Architecture lenses.

name: Musée Cernuschi
short_description: City of Paris museum of Asian arts opened in 1898 in the former mansion of banker Henri Cernuschi, holding nearly 15,000 Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese objects.
name_variations: Musée des Arts de l'Asie de la Ville de Paris
Asian Arts Museum of the City of Paris

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Second-largest Asian art collection in Paris after the Musee Guimet; permanent collections free to enter and the building sits at the eastern edge of Parc Monceau. Strong Hidden History and Religious & Spiritual lens potential.

name: Cathédrale Saint-Alexandre-Nevsky
short_description: Russian Orthodox cathedral consecrated in 1861, the first permanent Russian Orthodox place of worship in Paris, built in a Byzantine-Muscovite style with five gilded onion domes.

_pipeline.discovery_notes: Designed by Roman Kouzmine and Ivan Strohm of the St. Petersburg Academy and a long-time anchor of Paris's 'Little Russia' quarter near Parc Monceau; Pablo Picasso married Olga Khokhlova here in 1918. Distinctive Religious & Spiritual and Hidden History lens material.
